domain_restrictions: r is an integer with r at least 1
b_1 through b_r form a permutation of {1,...,r}
i ranges over integers from 1 to r minus 1
The condition on the permutation is alternating: when i is odd, b_{i+1} is greater than b_i, and when i is even, b_{i+1} is less than b_i
E_0 is assigned the value 1 by convention
n is an integer with n at least 2
j ranges over integers from 1 to n
The binomial coefficient is taken with parameters n minus 1 and j minus 1, so both are integers in the usual combinatorial range
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Define E_r for each positive integer r as the number of permutations of {1,...,r} whose entries alternate up and down, starting with an increase at the first step, and set E_0 to 1. For each integer n at least 2, define w_j as the binomial coefficient n minus 1 choose j minus 1 times E_{j-1} times E_{n-j}. Then, for that n, the sum of w_j over odd j from 1 to n equals E_n, and the sum of w_j over even j from 1 to n also equals E_n.
quantifier_order: For each integer r at least 1, define E_r by counting permutations b_1 through b_r of {1,...,r} satisfying the alternating sign inequalities, and also set E_0 equal to 1.
For the fixed integer n at least 2, define w_j for each j from 1 to n.
For that same fixed n, the sum of w_j over odd j equals E_n.
For that same fixed n, the sum of w_j over even j equals E_n.

witness_dependencies: The permutation counted by E_r is an implicit witness object depending on r, but E_r is defined as a count, not by selecting a specific permutation
w_j depends on the fixed n and on the previously defined values E_{j-1} and E_{n-j}
The parity restricted sums do not introduce any additional existential witnesses

statement_nl: For each integer r >= 1, let E_r be the number of permutations (b_1,...,b_r) of {1,...,r} such that (-1)^(i-1) * (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for every 1 <= i <= r-1, and set E_0 = 1. Fix an integer n >= 2 and define w_j = binom(n-1, j-1) * E_{j-1} * E_{n-j} for 1 <= j <= n. Then sum over odd j in {1,...,n} of w_j is equal to E_n, and sum over even j in {1,...,n} of w_j is also equal to E_n.
